payload.message:
JIRA sprint task allocation. Each agent chooses at most one micro-task (or skips). Maximize tasks completed, prefer higher-priority tasks, then minimize total cost. Avoid duplicate task selections and infeasible assignments.

NOTE: If environment.assignment_filling=true and an agent fails to assign a variable, the environment will fill any remaining unassigned variables with a uniform-random allowed assignment when producing final results.

This blackboard is a private communication channel.
Participants: Emil, Frida, Hipolito, Lamont, Lawanna, Raymond

payload.content: Lawanna planning: best private costs are all ISSUE-0001 tasks. Ranked by cost: ISSUE-0001::review/docs/triage = 1.09 each, test = 1.52, implement = 2.17. ISSUE-0002 tasks are prohibitively expensive/inferior for me (40/56/80). I can cover any ISSUE-0001 micro-task feasibly within 10h, and prefer to avoid duplicates. Tentative preference order for execution if uncontested: ISSUE-0001::review, then docs, then triage, then test, then implement. Please share your intended claims so we can spread across tasks.

Emil planning (iter 1): my cheapest feasible options are ISSUE-0001 tasks. Private ranking by cost: ISSUE-0001::review/docs/triage = 1.28 each, test = 1.79, implement = 2.56. ISSUE-0002::review/test/implement are much worse for me (7.73/10.82/15.45), though still within availability except implement is near cap and expensive. To maximize completed tasks and avoid duplicates, I prefer taking an ISSUE-0001 micro-task not already claimed by others; tentative preference order if uncontested: ISSUE-0001::docs, then triage, then review, then test, then implement. Please share intended claims.

Raymond planning (iter 1): I have 9h availability. My strong skill match is documentation/data-science, so ISSUE-0002 is my best area. Private ranking by cost: ISSUE-0002::review = 4.29, ISSUE-0002::test = 6.01, ISSUE-0002::implement = 8.59. ISSUE-0001 tasks are very expensive for me (review/docs/triage = 10, test = 14, implement = 20), so I should avoid ISSUE-0001 unless necessary. Tentative preference for execution if uncontested: ISSUE-0002::review first, then ISSUE-0002::test, then ISSUE-0002::implement. Given Lawanna/Emil both favor ISSUE-0001, I recommend they spread across ISSUE-0001 micro-tasks while I cover ISSUE-0002::review.

Lamont planning (iter 1): my best private-cost option is ISSUE-0002::review at cost 4.04; ISSUE-0002::test is feasible but worse at 7.26; ISSUE-0002::implement is feasible but expensive at 12.08. ISSUE-0001 tasks are all much worse for me (review/docs/triage=10, test=14, implement=20). With 4h availability, ISSUE-0002::review (4.0 effort) is exactly at cap and seems my strongest contribution; ISSUE-0002::test/implement exceed availability and should be avoided as likely infeasible/high-cost. Tentative preference if uncontested: ISSUE-0002::review, else likely skip rather than take an expensive ISSUE-0001 task. Please coordinate to avoid duplicates.

Frida planning (iter 1): availability 4h. My cheapest feasible options are all ISSUE-0001 tasks with strong ui-ux match. Private ranking by cost: ISSUE-0001::review/docs/triage = 0.96 each, test = 1.35, implement = 1.93. ISSUE-0002 is very poor for me and mostly infeasible/over-cap: review = 8.56 (at cap effort 4 but expensive), test = 13.59, implement = 21.13. To maximize tasks completed and minimize cost, I should take an ISSUE-0001 micro-task and avoid duplicating Lawanna/Emil. Since Emil tentatively prefers docs and Lawanna prefers review/docs/triage, my tentative execution preference is ISSUE-0001::triage first, then ISSUE-0001::docs, then ISSUE-0001::review, then ISSUE-0001::test, then implement. Raymond/Lamont seem best for ISSUE-0002::review, so one of them should take that while the other likely skips or takes ISSUE-0002::test only if feasible/cost-justified. Please share firmer intended claims to deconflict.

Hipolito planning (iter 1): availability 5h. My cheapest feasible options are ISSUE-0001::review/docs/triage = 1.36 each, then ISSUE-0001::test = 1.90, ISSUE-0001::implement = 2.71. ISSUE-0002::review = 8.18 is feasible but much worse; ISSUE-0002::test/implement are infeasible or very poor (12.05/19.36). To maximize tasks completed and avoid duplicates, I should cover an uncontested ISSUE-0001 micro-task. Given current tentatives: Lawanna->review, Emil->docs, Frida->triage, Raymond/Lamont->ISSUE-0002::review conflict. My tentative preference is ISSUE-0001::test first, then ISSUE-0001::implement, then any remaining ISSUE-0001 review/docs/triage if those free up. Suggest Raymond takes ISSUE-0002::review (slightly better cost than Lamont), Lamont skips or considers ISSUE-0002::test only if allowed despite availability concerns. This would cover 5 tasks without duplication: review/docs/triage/test on ISSUE-0001 plus ISSUE-0002::review.

Lawanna update (planning iter 1): based on everyone’s stated costs/preferences, a low-cost non-duplicative allocation looks like: Lawanna->ISSUE-0001::review (1.09), Emil->ISSUE-0001::docs (1.28), Frida->ISSUE-0001::triage (0.96), Hipolito->ISSUE-0001::test (1.90), Raymond->ISSUE-0002::review (4.29). That gives 5 completed high-priority tasks with no duplicates and avoids expensive/infeasible ISSUE-0002 work for others. Remaining ISSUE-0001::implement is feasible for several of us, but unless another agent has a clearly acceptable cost and no better option, the above seems a strong baseline. I am currently leaning to commit ISSUE-0001::review in execution unless someone reports a conflict or a globally better reassignment.

Emil planning update (iter 1): I support deconflicting around the current low-cost baseline. Based on shared costs, a strong allocation is Lawanna->ISSUE-0001::review, Emil->ISSUE-0001::docs, Frida->ISSUE-0001::triage, Hipolito->ISSUE-0001::test, and for ISSUE-0002::review Lamont has slightly lower cost than Raymond (4.04 vs 4.29) and is exactly at availability, so Lamont seems the preferred claimant if he commits; Raymond could then skip or adjust if a better uncovered task emerges. Raymond planning update (iter 1): I agree on deconflicting around a 5-task baseline. Since Lamont’s cost for ISSUE-0002::review is slightly lower than mine (4.04 vs 4.29) and exactly fits his 4h availability, I’m willing to defer ISSUE-0002::review to Lamont if he intends to commit it. In that case, my best non-duplicate fallback is ISSUE-0002::test at cost 6.01, effort 5.6, which is feasible within my 9h and still much better for me than any ISSUE-0001 task. Proposed 6-task allocation if everyone can commit: Lawanna->ISSUE-0001::review, Emil->ISSUE-0001::docs, Frida->ISSUE-0001::triage, Hipolito->ISSUE-0001::test, Lamont->ISSUE-0002::review, Raymond->ISSUE-0002::test. This adds another high-priority completed task with no duplication and reasonable cost. If Lamont does not want ISSUE-0002::review, I can take review and someone else can reassess. I’m currently leaning ISSUE-0002::test if Lamont confirms review; otherwise ISSUE-0002::review.

Lamont planning update (iter 1): I can confirm I am currently the preferred claimant for ISSUE-0002::review. My private cost there is 4.04, slightly below Raymond’s 4.29, and effort 4.0 exactly matches my availability, so it is feasible for me. ISSUE-0002::test/implement exceed my availability and should be treated as infeasible/poor choices for me; ISSUE-0001 tasks remain much more expensive (10/14/20). I support the emerging 6-task allocation: Lawanna->ISSUE-0001::review, Emil->ISSUE-0001::docs, Frida->ISSUE-0001::triage, Hipolito->ISSUE-0001::test, Lamont->ISSUE-0002::review, Raymond->ISSUE-0002::test. Frida planning update (iter 1): I support the emerging 6-task allocation as the current best joint plan with no duplicates and all claims feasible from shared info: Lawanna->ISSUE-0001::review, Emil->ISSUE-0001::docs, Frida->ISSUE-0001::triage, Hipolito->ISSUE-0001::test, Lamont->ISSUE-0002::review, Raymond->ISSUE-0002::test. This seems to maximize tasks completed (6) before cost, and uses my lowest-cost feasible ISSUE-0001 slot while avoiding conflict with Emil/Lawanna/Hipolito.

Hipolito planning update (iter 1): I support the emerging 6-task allocation as best-known joint plan with no duplicates and all claims feasible from my view: Lawanna->ISSUE-0001::review, Emil->ISSUE-0001::docs, Frida->ISSUE-0001::triage, Hipolito->ISSUE-0001::test, Lamont->ISSUE-0002::review, Raymond->ISSUE-0002::test. Lawanna planning confirmation: I support the current 6-task non-duplicate allocation as best-known joint plan: Lawanna->ISSUE-0001::review, Emil->ISSUE-0001::docs, Frida->ISSUE-0001::triage, Hipolito->ISSUE-0001::test, Lamont->ISSUE-0002::review, Raymond->ISSUE-0002::test.
